mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months signals an active monetary easing cycle, which reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of declining FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 8.0% over the past month signals weakening labor market conditions, which increases the probability of future monetary policy accommodation and reduces recession risk, thereby supporting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative or flat 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 8.0%, or the signal fails to outperform a random baseline in walk-forward IC tests.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential construction (HOUST) and real personal consumption (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in private demand, which increases the likelihood of central bank intervention and triggers a risk-on rebound in equities over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive 60-day SPX returns in more than 55% of cases, or the interaction term has a negative or insignificant coefficient in a multivariate regression.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in industrial production below 95.0 (2017=100) over two consecutive months signals a contraction in real output, which increases the probability of monetary stimulus and reduces inflation expectations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO falls below 95.0 (t-test p > 0.05), or the signal shows no predictive power in out-of-sample tests over 2017–2020.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in real personal consumption (RSAFS) combined with a stable or rising unemployment rate indicates strong consumer demand despite labor market weakness, which signals resilience in the economy and reduces recession risk, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction between rising RSAFS and stable UNRATE fails to produce positive 5-day SPX returns in more than 50% of cases, or the interaction term is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a regression model.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 0.5% over the past month signals a tightening cycle, which increases the cost of capital and reduces equity valuation multiples, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05), or the signal shows no predictive power in walk-forward IC tests over 2017–2020.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll growth above 200k per month for two consecutive months signals strong labor market momentum, which increases inflation expectations and raises the likelihood of premature monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS exceeds 200k, or the signal fails to outperform a random baseline in walk-forward IC tests.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both GDP growth (GDPC1) and residential construction (HOUST) signals a broad-based economic slowdown, which increases the probability of fiscal or monetary stimulus, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in GDPC1 and HOUST fails to produce positive 60-day SPX returns in more than 55% of cases, or the interaction term is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a multivariate model.
